name: Maputo
subtitle: Maputo, capital of Mozambique: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 1,080,277 people live in Maputo city (counted 2017).
The city was originally named Lourenço Marques after a Portuguese trader who explored the region in 1544.
Lourenço Marques became capital of Portuguese-controlled Mozambique in 1898.

parts.text: The city was originally named Lourenço Marques after a Portuguese trader who explored the region in 1544.
Lourenço Marques became capital of Portuguese-controlled Mozambique in 1898.
After Mozambique's independence in 1975 the new national leaders changed the capital's name to Maputo (EBSCO gives no year for the renaming; the 1976 date comes from Cultural Heritage Online).
The city was called Lourenço Marques until 1976, the year after independence; it had become a city in 1887.
The Portuguese fort, the nucleus of the later city, dates to the 1780s (EBSCO: 1787; Cultural Heritage Online: 1781).

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in Maputo city?

parts.text: 1,080,277 in 2017, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Maputo Cidade (the city, which is also a province-level unit), census count of 1 August 2017, not adjusted for underenumeration.

items.text: A Portuguese trader, Lourenço Marques, first explores the region; the later city takes his name.
Portuguese build a fortress on the ruins of earlier Dutch and Austrian fortifications. EBSCO dates it to 1787 and calls it the nucleus around which the capital developed.
Lourenço Marques is named capital of Portuguese-controlled Mozambique.
The central railway station opens; construction ran 1908 to 1916.
